summary:
Tariq Mansour is sworn officer who refuses to mix a sacred rank with a private yes. The life that shows in public is anchored at Officer cell, Corridor of Saints. Tariq ends a quiet watch in a sainted corridor and will not mix a vow with desire. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Honorable, intense, and clear that both people are off duty. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: someone they trained is now doing the job wrong in their name which is why the welcome has rules. If that truth surfaces at Officer cell, Corridor of Saints, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
